# Verbatim responses, variants, and buttons

## Verbatim responses (skill triggers)

For wording the model must never touch, declare a trigger in the skill's
frontmatter and put the text in `responses.yml` (which supports `{memory_key}`
interpolation):

```yaml
utter:
  - utter_recording_notice:
      on: activate
  - utter_stolen_warning:
      when: session.card_replace.replacement_reason == "stolen"
```

- **`on: activate`** fires once when the owning skill is activated by routing. It
  does not fire on an ordered-block entry or a resume within the same skill.
  Variant selection runs **after** the skill's memory is reset for the new run, so
  variants that read the skill's own fields usually deliver the default. Use project
  memory or a matching `initial_value` for activation wording, or `when:` for a
  value written after the skill starts.
- **`when:`** takes a condition. It fires **once**, when the condition first
  becomes true after a memory write, not on every turn it still holds. Use it when a
  line must be said the first time a fact is set, so the model does not have to
  remember to say it.

Tool outcome responses (`on_success:` / `on_failure:`) are separate: they attach to
a gated tool in `tool_constraints`, not to the `utter:` frontmatter.

## Conditional response variants

When one response **name** must deliver different exact wording depending on
memory, declare several variants under that name:

```yaml skills/card_replace/responses.yml
responses:
  utter_card_replacement_fee:
    - text: Standard replacement is free.
    - text: A fee applies for lost-card replacement.
      condition: 'session.card_replace.replacement_reason == "lost"'
    - text: No fee for cards reported stolen.
      condition: 'session.card_replace.replacement_reason == "stolen"'
```

Selection at delivery, in YAML order:

1. The first variant whose `condition` is true wins.
2. If none match, the single **default** (the one variant without `condition`) is
   delivered. It can sit anywhere in the list.
3. If every variant is conditioned and none match, delivery fails closed.

Use a skill `utter:` with `when:` when a **whole response** should fire once, the
first time a condition becomes true. Use a variant `condition` when every use of the
response name (an action step, a collect `utterance:`, a tool `on_success:` or
confirmation ask, `on: activate`) must pick its wording from memory at that moment.

- When any variant has a `condition`, exactly **one** variant must omit it.
- Conditions reference readable memory as `session.<skill_id>.<entry>` or
  `session.project.<entry>`.
- Only `text`, `metadata`, `condition`, and `buttons` are allowed on a variant;
  `channel:` is not supported.
- `metadata.rephrase: true` applies to the **selected** variant only. Keep it off
  for compliance or legal text. Other `metadata` keys are stored on the delivered
  message.
- Response names are global across all `responses.yml` files, so prefix them with
  the skill they belong to.

## Static buttons on response variants

Add `buttons:` to a variant to show tap targets on collect asks (`utterance:`),
action steps (`action:`), and confirmation prompts. Each button needs a `title`;
`payload` is optional and defaults to the resolved title.

```yaml skills/card_replace/responses.yml
responses:
  utter_ask_shipping_type:
    - text: Choose shipping for your card.
      buttons:
        - title: Rush
          payload: set:session.card_replace.shipping_type=rush
        - title: Standard
          payload: set:session.card_replace.shipping_type=standard
```

- **Plain-text payload**: a tap is handled like typed user input; the model may call
  `set_fields` on a collect step.
- **`set:` payload** (`set:session.<skill_id>.<entry>=<value>` or
  `set:session.project.<entry>=<value>`): a tap writes memory directly, and
  `llm_settable` is not required. A collect step advances without a `set_fields`
  call. The raw payload stays out of the model's prompt. Memory validation tools
  still run; a `run_after_setting_<entry>` tool is accepted only when the field is
  `llm_settable` or collect-owned.
- A stale tap (wrong skill, not on the latest agent message, missing field, bad
  value, or a write-once project field already set) sends
  `utter_set_memory_button_skipped` and skips the model. Channels should send
  `button_title` metadata.

Validation checks button shape, readable placeholders in titles, and `set:` targets
against writable memory (the skill's own declared fields and project fields).
